Councillors voted 9-4 on Tuesday night to approve a 1.2bn waterfront scheme, ending three years of debate.

The plan covers 40 hectares of former dock land and includes 3,500 homes, a new tram line and a public park along the river.

Opponents argued the scheme would price out existing residents. "We asked for a guarantee on affordable units and we did not get one," said councillor Priya Nair.

Construction is expected to begin in 2026.

Cranes over the old harbour. Photograph: A. Reporter

Councillors voted 9-4 on Tuesday night to approve a 1.2bn waterfront scheme, ending three years of debate.

The plan covers 40 hectares of former dock land and includes 3,500 homes, a new tram line and a public park along the river.

Opponents argued the scheme would price out existing residents. "We asked for a guarantee on affordable units and we did not get one," said councillor Priya Nair.

Construction is expected to begin in 2026.
